kb_description: Canonical Open Knowledge Format (OKF v0.2) repository: separating operational & system reality ('What Is') from proposed product innovations ('What Could Be').

categories.title: Production Systems & Architecture ('What Is')
categories.description: Active production software, backend services, client apps, data stores, and internal workflows.

categories.title: External Ecosystem & Industry Reality ('What Is')
categories.description: External regulatory environment, industry standards, third-party APIs, and partner rails.

categories.title: Concepts, Thematic Clusters & Proposals
categories.description: Theoretical constructs, architectural RFCs, foundational models, thematic concept clusters, and exploratory initiatives.

categories.title: Frontier & Emerging Ideas ('What Could Be')
categories.description: Exploratory horizon-scanning initiatives, emerging prototypes, experimental ideas, and nascent proposals.

categories.title: Visual Storyboards & User Journeys ('What Could Be')
categories.description: Sequential visual narrative storyboards illustrating product features, user journeys, and partner integrations.

categories.title: Audio Overviews & Podcasts ('What Could Be')
categories.description: NotebookLM-style two-host deep dive audio overviews, conversational breakdowns, and synthetic podcast episodes.

categories.title: Operational Playbooks & Runbooks
categories.description: Standard operating procedures, incident guides, and team runbooks.

categories.title: Field Research & User Interviews
categories.description: Customer interviews, field observations, survey data, and qualitative provenance.

categories.title: Agent Skills & Automation Capabilities
categories.description: Reusable AI agent capabilities, maintenance tools, and automation workflows.

categories.title: Standards, Specifications & References
categories.description: Format specifications, schemas, data contracts, and knowledge base audit logs.

categories.title: Knowledge Document Starter Templates
categories.description: Standardized templates for creating new concepts, systems, playbooks, and research notes.
